I farm wheat and maize on the same 16.1 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will use the full 16.1 mu for wheat in the winter season and then the same 16.1 mu for maize in the summer season. I have 40 years of experience, I only have a two-person household, and I have well irrigation, so I will aim for a steady, practical plan that I know I can carry through without taking unnecessary risk. For wheat, I will use an improved variety rather than old traditional seed because I want stable emergence, lodging resistance, and a dependable grain yield. I will keep fertilizer at a moderate-to-strong level because my land is irrigated and wheat responds well when water and nutrients match. I will irrigate three times if the season is normal, because in my area wheat usually needs water at key stages. I will use rotary tillage for wheat because after maize harvest I want a workable seedbed and reliable stand establishment. For maize, I will plant a hybrid because that is what I trust most for yield on my irrigated land. Since wheat harvest and maize sowing are tight together, I will keep maize establishment simple and fast, and I will use no-tillage to save time and labor and to protect soil moisture. I will still feed maize well, but I will not push inputs too aggressively because I value stable returns more than chasing the highest possible yield. I will keep pesticide use limited to what I think is necessary to protect the crop, not more.
